report.title: Stratified human spot-audit of benchmark verdicts, with an escalation threshold
report.question: Implementation target: mirror the Phase-11 rule at :11041 - sample the platform's own verdicts, re-adjudicate them by hand, and if the sampled error rate exceeds a pre-set threshold, expand re-verification to the entire affected class. Stratify the sample by oracle type (deterministic versus judged) and by verdict (pass versus fail), because a platform that is accurate on passes and wrong on failures has a specific, fixable bias that an unstratified sample averages away.
report.answer: Sample design first: 2x2 strata (oracle_type × platform_verdict), equal n=8 per stratum, seed=3230323, selection=sort-then-shuffle-with-stratum-derived-rng. Frozen synthetic ledger n=80 because command-center/bench/results/ is absent (live_results_usable=True). Per-stratum Wilson 95% intervals follow that design. judged:fail sampled error rate=0.625 exceeds pre-registered threshold 0.1 (boundary=strict_gt, recorded_at=2026-08-24T18:00:00Z); full-class re-verification enqueued for ['deterministic:fail', 'judged:fail', 'judged:pass']. deterministic:pass sampled rate=0, so the pass/fail bias is visible only because the sample is stratified. TST-0309 present=False. SUCCESS:TST-0323

sample_design.allocation: equal n_per_stratum drawn independently inside each of the four oracle_type × platform_verdict strata
sample_design.selection_method: Within each stratum, sort case_id lexicographically, shuffle with random.Random(int(sha256(utf8(frame_seed || '|' || stratum_id))[:16], 16)), take the first n_per_stratum ids. The draw is a function of (seed, population, stratum), not a hand-picked list.
sample_design.stratum_definition: cartesian product oracle_type ∈ {deterministic, judged} × platform_verdict ∈ {fail, pass}. Every ledger row lands in exactly one stratum.
sample_design.why_before_rates: An error rate from a convenience sample is not an error rate. Strata, sizes, seed and selection method are recorded here before any k/n is reported.
